route: Long Term Entry Permit, on the employer's Immigrant Employment Certificate

permit.applies: The employer (any person engaged in a trade, profession or vocation in St Helena) applies to the Immigration Control Board for the Immigrant Employment Certificate; each immigrant employee holds a Long Term Entry Permit.
permit.first: The Board's regard to the local labour market and the specialist skills sought, and the employer's arrangements for accommodation, health, welfare and repatriation.

fees.what: Short Term Entry Permit, on arrival (for a stay under 183 days)

sources.title: Immigration Ordinance 2011, consolidated to 1 April 2021 (St Helena Government)
sources.said: who has been present in St Helena for less than 183 days in the period of one year preceding the day on which the work is done. … An application for an immigrant employment certificate may be made by any person engaged in any trade, profession or vocation in St Helena who wishes to employ one or more immigrants in that business, and must be made to the Board in the approved form. … the name of the employer and the period (which must not exceed 5 years) of its operation;

sources.title: St Helena Government, Immigrant Employment Certificate
sources.said: An Immigrant Employment Certificate is required by an employer to employ immigrants in St Helena and can be valid for a period of one to five years. … Each immigrant employee must hold a Long Term Entry Permit and pass Points Based System

sources.title: St Helena Government, Long Term Entry Permit
sources.said: The Long-term Entry Permit is issuable for a period not exceeding five years.

sources.title: St Helena Government, Requirements for Short Term Entry Permits
sources.said: An entry fee of GBP £20.00 is chargeable … applies on arrival, for permission to enter St Helena for a period not exceeding 183 days

sources.title: Immigration (Amendment) Ordinance 2026, No. 4 of 2026
sources.said: This Ordinance comes into force on a date fixed by the Governor by Order. … may lawfully work in St Helena unless they hold a valid permission to stay and work permit.

note: Under the Immigration Ordinance 2011 (s. 23(1)(c)), 'employment' doesn't include work done by a person present in St Helena for less than 183 days in the year before the day the work is done, so a performer staying under 183 days works on the Short Term Entry Permit alone (taken as 182 in 365). The certificate runs one to five years and the Long Term Entry Permit up to five. The Immigration (Amendment) Ordinance 2026 (No. 4, gazetted 3 August 2026) would remove that exclusion and the certificate, replacing both with a 'permission to stay and work permit', but it comes into force only on a date the Governor fixes by Order, and no such Order was found (2026-11-01).
